function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

I don’t have direct visibility into your current connection, so I can’t tell you the exact download/upload speeds right now. Here’s how you can quickly find out yourself: | Method | What to do | |--------|------------| | **Web‑based Speed Test** | • Go to (or simply search “SpeedTest” in Google – the first result will launch the same page).
- Click **Go**.
- Wait while the site measures latency, download, and upload rates. | | **Built‑in Windows Tool** | • Press Win+R → type `ncpa.cpl` → Enter.
- Right‑click your active Ethernet/Wi‑Fi adapter → **Status…**.
- In the Status window click **Details…** – you’ll see *Bytes Received* / *Bytes Sent*. If you keep the window open long enough, you can calculate approximate throughput. | | **Command Line (Windows)** | ```powershell\nInvoke-WebRequest -Uri https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sivel/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py -OutFile .\speedtest.py\npython .\speedtest.py\n```
This uses the popular `speedtest-cli` script. You’ll need PowerShell & Python preinstalled. | | **Mac/Linux Terminal** | ```bash\ncurl -sL https://install.speedtest.net/app/cli/install.sh | sudo bash\nsudo apt-get install --reinstall speedtest # Debian/Ubuntu
\nspeedtest\n```\n(Or use Homebrew on macOS: `brew install speedtest`). | ### Quick Tips 1. **Run at least twice** – one quick test gives a snapshot; another after a few minutes shows consistency. 2. **Close other bandwidth‑heavy apps** before testing (streaming video, downloads) to get a clean measurement. 3. **Check both directions** – most plans advertise only download speed; upload matters too for uploads, cloud backups, gaming, etc. If you’d prefer me to run a test from this chat interface, let me know—though note that many environments where assistants run aren’t connected to the public Internet, so the results might not reflect your real home/network conditions.
